title: What is the contract between equals() and hashCode()?
shortTitle: What is the contract between equals() and hashCode()?
keyPoints: If two objects are equal by equals(), they MUST have the same hashCode()
If two objects have the same hashCode(), they are NOT necessarily equal (hash collision)
Breaking this contract breaks HashMap and HashSet – objects become unfindable
equals() contract: reflexive, symmetric, transitive, consistent, null returns false
hashCode() contract: consistent during the object's lifetime, same for equal objects

s1_definition.oneliner: If a.equals(b) is true, then a.hashCode() must equal b.hashCode(). Breaking this contract makes objects unfindable in HashMap and HashSet.
s1_definition.profdef:
The contract:

- **equals() true → hashCode() must be same.** Required for HashMap/HashSet.
- **hashCode() same → equals() may or may not be true.** Hash collisions are allowed.
- **If you override equals(), you must override hashCode().** Breaking this rule is the #1 cause of "HashMap lost my object" bugs.
s1_definition.analogy: The bank files accounts in a cabinet by the first letter of the account holder's name (hashCode). Two people with the same name hash to the same drawer. If equals says two accounts are the same but they hash to different drawers, the bank can never find the second one.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Contract:
    a.equals(b) == true  →  a.hashCode() == b.hashCode()  (REQUIRED)
    a.hashCode() == b.hashCode()  →  a.equals(b) may or may not be true  (collision OK)

  HashMap:
    put(key, value) → bucket = hashCode % capacity → store in bucket
    get(key) → bucket = hashCode % capacity → scan bucket with equals

  Broken hashCode → wrong bucket → equals never checked → object lost
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
The equals-hashCode contract says: if two objects are equal by equals(), they must have the same hashCode(). Breaking this rule makes objects unfindable in HashMap and HashSet because the lookup goes to the wrong bucket.

Always override both together. Use the same fields in both methods. Use Objects.hash() for convenience, or let records and Lombok generate them.

One sentence to remember: equal objects must have equal hash codes – break this and HashMap loses your data.
